verdicts.summary: The main hazard in this note is finding 0: everything before closeRun is unbounded (the mutex wait, onShutdown, the restartFiber interrupt). The rest checks out. closeRun forks the close into parentScope and races it against timeoutOption(5s), returning false on timeout. stop() then returns early. markComplete still runs via Effect.ensuring. DesktopUpdates uses the same pattern.
When the 5s budget trips, nothing is logged. Before this change the user-quit path never timed out, so it never had this gap.
verdicts.scenario: 1. A backend's run-scope finalizer hangs, for example the child ignores SIGTERM and the drain stalls. 2. The user quits. 3. stopAllPoolInstances calls stop({timeout: 5s}). 4. closeRun's timeoutOption fires and returns false (DesktopBackendManager.ts:368). 5. stop returns at :1088-1089 without logging and without clearing state.active. 6. The app quits and the process exits. The child may be orphaned, and no log says which backend hung or that the budget ran out.
verdicts.consequence: An operator can't diagnose quits that hang or leave orphaned backend processes. There's no log line for the timeout and none naming the instance.

verdicts.summary: The open question is settled: the WSL backend's config step does run prepareRuntime while start() holds the mutex. The chain is DesktopWslBackend.ts:165 configResolve = configuration.resolveWsl → DesktopBackendConfiguration.ts:862 resolveWslStartConfig → :599 runWslPreflight → :363 wslEnv.prepareRuntime. start() holds the mutex across configResolve (DesktopBackendManager.ts:692, :711), and stop() waits on that same mutex at :1051. This is exactly the hang in finding 0.

After a timeout, the run is left in state.active. When the layer scope is torn down later, its finalizer calls stop() with no timeout. That call goes through closeRun's unbounded path and awaits run.fiber, which is still stuck on the hung teardown. So the Effect layer teardown in runMain can hang. Whether the process still exits depends on Electron's app.quit ending the process no matter what Node work is pending.
verdicts.scenario: 1. The quit finalizer times out and markComplete fires. 2. DesktopLifecycle's finally() calls electronApp.quit. 3. scopedProgram returns and runMain starts tearing down the layer scope. 4. The finalizer at DesktopBackendManager.ts:1157 calls stop(). 5. stop() takes the mutex, finds the run still active, and calls closeRun with no timeout (:362-363). 6. Fiber.await(run.fiber) blocks on the hung run-scope finalizer.
verdicts.missing: How Electron's app.quit and process exit behave while NodeRuntime.runMain is still running layer finalizers. That is runtime behaviour I can't read in the checkout. The effect library source isn't vendored either, so I couldn't confirm the forkIn/interrupt ordering on parentScope close.
